# Ecosystem reference fixture

Synthetic original intake data and FLO source; no customer records. FLO 0.5.0's
public `flo.export()` generated `process-export.json` from `baseline.flo`. The
installed-package test reproduces that export using the pinned published release.

The synthetic model separates review work from its routing decision. FLO 0.5
profiles use explicitly declared planned basis and selectors for its original
synthetic durations; items now live under process and handoff/rework are objects.
Observation identities, timings and the independently drawn observed PNG remain
unchanged. Original exports/sources are retained in `legacy-0.4.2/` and
`legacy-0.4.3/` for backward-compatible restoration.

The `.flo` source declares parallel reviews, explicit review rework/handoff and
modeled durations in minutes. Observations use source activity codes, leading-zero
case IDs, interleaved ordering, repeated review events and an incomplete case.
Required cohort boundaries are explicitly intake and close observations; case 003
is excluded because close is absent. These are observed spans and do not establish
full path conformance or business-calendar working time.

`expected.json` is independently hand-calculated:

- Case 002 spans 08:00–13:00 = 5 hours; case 001 spans 08:00–12:00 = 4 hours.
  First source occurrence orders them 002, 001. Mean span is 4.5 hours.
- Review occurrences last 1, 0.5, 2 hours; their mean is 7/6 hours. Approval lasts
  1 and 0.5 hours (mean 0.75). Intake and close each have two 1-hour observations.
- Modeled intake remains 20 minutes; it is never replaced by observed mean 1 hour.

`observed-lead-time.png` is a visually inspected reference drawn directly from
fixed positions [0, 1], values [5, 4] and labels [002, 001], using Matplotlib 3.11.2,
Seaborn 0.13.2's local whitegrid style, DejaVu Sans, 6.4×4.8 inches, 100 dpi and
constrained layout. It includes the explicit exclusion message. Agg lays out the
figure once; layout is frozen before export. Its construction did not invoke
LSS4PY calculations or `plot_timing`. The fixture is changed only after semantic
checks and visual review, never automatically regenerated by the test.

Schema/semantic acceptance uses exact comparisons plus numeric tolerances.
PNG comparison allows RMS 0.5 for small rasterization differences; it complements
exact artist values/labels and text-bounds checks rather than establishing numbers.
